content:
maria.ops: Heads up — asia-east1 routing flap. A subset of edge nodes are reporting high packet loss to GPU backend pools and we triggered the automated partial failover to eu-west at 08:05 UTC. Noticing a lot of client errors because resolvers are still returning the old A records (long-lived caches).

jonathan.eng: Confirmed. We performed a staggered CNAME rotation instead of wholesale A swap to avoid immediate mass reconnects. Change applied at 08:05: `failover-asia.rw-inference.net -> failover-eu-west.rw-inference.net` (CNAME). deploy-bot posted the txn ID.

ben.networks: Dig shows many public resolvers still returning the asia A with ~1800s TTL remaining. Looks like the previous TTL was 1h; that explains the lag. Sample:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> failover-asia.rw-inference.net @8.8.8.8
;; ANSWER SECTION:
failover-asia.rw-inference.net. 1723 IN A 203.0.113.45
```

sre-oncall: Oof. We didn't have time to lower the TTL before the incident. Two notes: 1) lowering TTL now will only affect new records after the authoritative change — won't flush remote caches. 2) We can speed client convergence by priming caches and using targeted CDN/edge purge where available.

maria.ops: Action plan proposed:
- Lower authoritative TTL to 30s for the failover aliases (immediate).
- Prime major public resolvers / CDNs by issuing health-check requests from multiple egress IPs (script below).
- For corporate customers with sticky resolvers, send PS notice and provide the new endpoint IPs for manual whitelisting if needed.
- Divert non-critical batch GPU jobs to us-central to free asia capacity and reduce time-to-recover costs.

jonathan.eng: Script to prime caches (run from 10+ egress IPs / CI runners):```bash
for IP in $(cat egress_ips.txt); do
  curl -s -H "Host: failover-asia.rw-inference.net" http://edge-proxy.example --resolve "failover-asia.rw-inference.net:80:203.0.113.45" &
done
wait
```
This hits edges to create entries; also send Cloudflare purge for the alias if the customer uses it.

ben.networks: Also started an AS-path steering rule to prefer eu-west for traffic where BGP sessions still show asia path flaps. That should reduce backend load while DNS convergence happens. Monitor delta in connection counts to the asia GPU pools.

sre-oncall: Quick tip — for customers behind resolvers that obey DNS TTLs, a lowered TTL + priming should converge in ~1-3 minutes for compliant resolvers. For those behind ISP caches (which ignore TTLs occasionally), fallback is:
- short-term L7 redirect from the old A IPs to the new region (we can put a lightweight proxy there to return 302 to the new hostname), or
- announce a targeted anycast route (expensive; last resort).

maria.ops: We're starting the TTL change now: setting SOA/records to 30s. Estimated time: changes propagate to authoritative in ~10s. Reminder: this will not invalidate existing node caches.

deploy-bot: Automated failover job #fdo-298 applied: CNAME rotate + TTL update. See https://console.redwood/infrastructure/ops/txn/fdo-298

jonathan.eng: Also enabling short-lived health-check redirects on the asia A IPs to return 302 -> https://failover-eu-west.rw-inference.net for HTTP flows. This will help browser/HTTP clients that hit the old IP. Non-HTTP protocols will still depend on DNS or BGP.

ben.networks: CPU/GPU note: we've offloaded ~40% of non-prod rendering to us-central GPUs; this reduced pressure on asia nodes immediately and avoided preempting p99 customer jobs. Cost impact: ~+$0.6/hr for cross-region egress during spill; much cheaper than emergency burst capacity.

sre-oncall: Monitoring checklist updated in the thread:
- Asia GPU pool error rate (RPC 5xx)
- Connection counts per region (edge -> backend)
- DNS authoritative query rate and response code breakdown
- Top 10 client resolvers still returning old A records (we'll DM them)

maria.ops: Early results: after priming and TTL set to 30s, our synthetic probes show 85% of probes now resolve to eu-west within 90s. Some large ISPs still at old A for ~20min. Tracking those in the board.

jonathan.eng: Note for post-incident: update runbooks to always pre-stage low TTLs for failover aliases during scheduled maintenance windows. Also add a small global priming job that runs automatically whenever we change failover records.

sre-oncall: Adding action items to follow-up:
- Run BGP path audit for the affected IXes (ben)
- Add global priming job to infra repo (jonathan)
- Customer comms draft for sticky resolver cases (maria)

maria.ops: Thanks all. Will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

ben.networks: FYI — I opened a ticket with the biggest ISP we saw (AS64500) asking them to clear the stale cache. They responded acknowledging and will monitor.

sre-oncall: Closing note — if you see lingering p99 latency, consider enabling the EU warm pool for a longer window in the short term. We may also want to automate graceful draining in the future to avoid sudden reconnections.

maria.ops: 2026-03-18 11:43 UTC — incident in steady state; continuing monitoring and follow-ups assigned.
